items.claim: OpenDB is a BSD-3 physical-design database based on LEF/DEF, supports fast binary save/load, persistent object IDs across save/restore, and exact-state comparison.
items.limits: OID persistence applies within save/restore of one database, not across independent place/post-route imports.

items.claim: OpenDB exposes bool/string/int/double dbProperty objects on database objects.
items.limits: Scalar named properties are not by themselves a versioned multi-producer annotation/provenance model.

items.claim: OpenROAD can read LEF/DEF or Verilog, link a design, and read/write binary OpenDB databases through Tcl; Python support is more limited for Verilog.
items.limits: Commercial Innovus export fidelity still requires a real AES import test.

items.claim: HAL provides a graph-based gate-level netlist core, Verilog/VHDL and Liberty parsers, C++/Python APIs, plugins, project persistence and an igraph graph-algorithm plugin under MIT.
items.limits: HAL is oriented to hardware reverse engineering and does not natively provide our DEF/SPEF/SDC commercial timing model.

items.claim: HAL's graph plugin converts gates/nets into an igraph-backed NetlistGraph and maps graph vertices back to gates.
items.limits: Multi-sink nets are translated into multiple edges; our DIG must retain hyperedge identity separately.

items.claim: HAL can store gate placement coordinates when its gate-library data mapping is configured.
items.limits: Placement metadata is not a replacement for a complete DEF/route/parasitic database.

items.claim: HAL has a resynthesis plugin that can resynthesize selected subgraphs through Yosys against a target library.
items.limits: The plugin is opt-in, requires Yosys, destroys original correspondence on subgraph resynthesis, and its target library must be a subset of the imported library.

items.claim: HAL has no prebuilt binaries, officially tests Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 and treats macOS support as experimental.
items.limits: This raises adoption/build cost for our macOS plus Rocky/Alma environment.

items.claim: OpenTimer reads Liberty, Verilog, SDC and SPEF, exposes graph/path timing and incremental C++ APIs, and uses MIT licensing.
items.limits: It is a timing engine, not a physical database or annotation store; feature/correlation coverage versus Innovus must be measured.

items.claim: iSTA reads DEF/Verilog, SDC, SPEF/SDF and Liberty and supports NLDM/Elmore plus CCS/AOCV-related analysis features.
items.limits: iEDA is a much larger integrated infrastructure and was not found installed locally; API and import fidelity require a separate build POC.

items.claim: iEDA provides an integrated database/platform/tool infrastructure under MulanPSL-2.0 and uses iDB to read LEF/DEF for physical tools.
items.limits: The integrated scope can duplicate Innovus/OpenDB responsibilities and increase adoption cost.

items.claim: UHDM/Surelog provides a serializable IEEE SystemVerilog/VPI elaborated object model with C++ navigation.
items.limits: It targets HDL elaboration, not post-route physical/timing data, so it is not a DIG core candidate.

items.claim: SQLite includes deterministic JSON functions by default in current releases, JSONB storage, R*Tree spatial indexing and recursive CTE support.
items.limits: SQLite is not an EDA parser and complex graph analytics normally need an in-memory graph projection or extension.

items.claim: LadybugDB is an active MIT-licensed embedded property graph database with Cypher, columnar storage, CSR adjacency and Python/Node/C++ binaries.
items.limits: It is a young Kuzu successor and has no EDA object model; deterministic evidence export and schema evolution need validation.

items.claim: Kuzu is archived and read-only as of October 2025, despite its attractive embedded property-graph feature set.
items.limits: Existing releases remain usable, but an archived dependency is unsuitable for a new core.

items.claim: Linglong's existing celluzi/IIC-OSIC container provides OpenROAD 26Q2-2270-g4c26918f5, OpenSTA, Yosys and Python-enabled OpenDB; dbProperty bindings are callable.
items.limits: Version availability is verified; import of our retained proprietary AES exports has not yet been run.

items.claim: The current macOS Python environment includes SQLite 3.51.0 with JSON and RTree, while python-igraph, NetworkX and DuckDB are not installed.
items.limits: Missing packages can be bundled later; this observation only describes the current host.

items.claim: OpenSTA exposes a timing-graph based STA engine, standard timing inputs, incremental updates and a Network Adapter API for an external netlist database.
items.limits: API capability does not establish numerical or ranking correlation with Innovus on the retained AES design.
